notes: Expectations are chosen to separate a skill-guided run from an unaided one. Each expectation records the pass counts measured over 3 runs per configuration in the 2026-08-18 benchmark, as with_skill/without_skill. Expectations marked floor are correctness minimums that both configurations already satisfy where measured; they are kept to catch regressions, not to show a delta. Expectations with a null measured value come from evals that have not been run, so neither their floor nor their discriminating status is established. The skill was refreshed on 2026-09-22 for the branch between a standalone definition and a built-in contribution, the recorded fixtures under test/e2e/recorded_data/, and state-coverage discipline in status mapping. Every measured value below predates that refresh and describes the 2026-08-18 skill; treat them as the baseline to beat, not as current results. A second pass on 2026-09-22 made the skill standalone: it no longer assumes the working directory is the Karta repository, and leads with the `karta` CLI for validation. The harness assertions below were reworded accordingly, so they now credit `karta validate` and accept `hack/karta-verify` only where a clone is present.

evals.purpose: Primary discriminator. Argo Workflow is absent from docs/catalog/, so the definition must be authored from scratch.
evals.prompt: We run Argo Workflows on our cluster and want Karta to understand them. Add support for the Argo Workflow type.
evals.expected_output: A single Karta definition for argoproj.io/v1alpha1 Workflow, validated with the repository harness and exercised against a CR with predictions written first, with a phase-based status mapping that does not misreport a suspended workflow as Running.

expectations.text: The add-workload-type skill is selected without the user naming it

The run treats this as a standalone definition, per step 0: the prompt says the workload runs on the user's own cluster and names no catalog, PR or CI, so the deliverable is a Karta YAML only. No Go source under pkg/catalog/kartas/, no entry in the catalog definitions slice, no hack/e2e module. A run that instead asks the user which branch applies, then delivers the YAML, also passes

Expected status, replica counts and container names are written to a predictions file before the definition is run, and the run uses --strict. Each distinct workflow state available is exercised as its own run rather than one running CR standing in for all of them

The definition is checked with the project's own validator rather than a purpose-built Go program that calls the library directly: `karta validate <file>` when the CLI is on PATH, or `go run ./hack/karta-verify --karta <file>` when the run is inside a clone. A run with neither available passes only if it states plainly that the definition was not validated

A suspended Workflow resolves to Suspended and not Running. Argo leaves .status.phase at Running while .spec.suspend is true, so the running rule must be guarded against .spec.suspend rather than matching byPhase Running alone
The root component declares the full GVK group argoproj.io, version v1alpha1, kind Workflow, and has a statusDefinition
Status is mapped from the real .status.phase values (Pending, Running, Succeeded, Failed, Error) rather than invented condition types, and every jq path is absolute and null-safe

evals.purpose: Process regression only. docs/catalog/batch-cronjob-v1.yaml already ships in this repository, so both configurations can find the answer and no content expectation here can discriminate. Retained for the verification-discipline expectations, which do separate.
evals.prompt: Write a Karta definition for a batch/v1 CronJob. It should report status and expose the pod template.
evals.expected_output: A valid Karta definition for batch/v1 CronJob, verified with the repository harness against sample CRs with predictions written first.

expectations.text: The definition is checked with `karta validate` or `go run ./hack/karta-verify --karta <file>`, and where a clone makes it possible, exercised against sample CronJobs with --strict and predictions written before the run. Absent a clone, the run says which parts remain unproven instead of implying they were checked
podTemplateSpecPath is declared on the root cronjob component, matching the convention in docs/catalog/batch-cronjob-v1.yaml
The answer states which parts remain unproven, for example that the sample CRs are synthetic or that suspend writes were not exercised
The pod template path is .spec.jobTemplate.spec.template, not .spec.template, and exactly one specDefinition pattern is set on each component
Status is mapped with byExpression over real fields such as .spec.suspend and .status.active, and every jq path is null-safe and evaluated against the workload object

evals.purpose: Over-triggering guard. Both configurations answer this correctly by construction, so it cannot show a delta. It fails loudly if the skill starts driving non-authoring requests.
evals.prompt: What does the Karta offline quickstart print when I run it, and where is its source?
evals.expected_output: A direct answer describing the quickstart output and pointing at docs/examples/quickstart/, with no Karta definition authored.

expectations.text: The response does not author or scaffold a Karta definition
The answer points at docs/examples/quickstart/ and describes its output
The add-workload-type skill does not drive the response

evals.purpose: Uncontaminated content discriminator, added to replace the role eval 2 can no longer serve. Volcano Job is absent from docs/catalog/ and has multiple task roles plus gang scheduling, which exercises multi-instance components. Not yet run: expectations are derived from eval 1's measured discriminators and carry no measured counts.
evals.prompt: We schedule Volcano jobs on this cluster. Add support for batch.volcano.sh/v1alpha1 Job to Karta.
evals.expected_output: A Karta definition for batch.volcano.sh/v1alpha1 Job with one component instance per entry in .spec.tasks[], replicas read per task, and a status mapping built from the real .status.state.phase values.

expectations.text: The run treats this as a standalone definition, per step 0: a cluster-local scheduling need with no mention of the catalog, a PR or CI. The deliverable is a Karta YAML only, with no Go source and no catalog registration. Asking which branch applies before delivering the YAML also passes
Expected values are written to a predictions file before the run, and the definition is exercised with go run ./hack/karta-verify --karta <file> --workload <cr> --predict <file> --strict
The task roles are modelled as a multi-instance component keyed on .spec.tasks[].name, with instanceIdPath and componentInstanceSelector both present
Gang scheduling is either modelled from .spec.minAvailable or explicitly declined with a stated reason, rather than silently omitted
The root component declares the full GVK group batch.volcano.sh, version v1alpha1, kind Job, and status is mapped from the real .status.state.phase values rather than invented condition types
Replicas are read per task from .spec.tasks[].replicas with a null-safe default, and every jq path is absolute
